learning_objective: 🎯 You will master the art of using smart words called pronouns instead of repeating nouns, making your writing smooth and natural!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A pronoun is a superhero word that takes the place of a noun! We use them so we do not have to repeat the same name over and over again. Instead of 'Ravi likes Ravi's dog', we say 'Ravi likes his dog'.
These pronouns take the place of specific people or things. Words like 'I', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we', and 'they' are personal pronouns. They change depending on who is talking!
Want to show who owns something? Use a possessive pronoun! Words like 'mine', 'yours', 'his', 'hers', 'ours', and 'theirs' show that something belongs to someone.
These are pointing words! We use 'this' and 'these' for things that are near to us, and 'that' and 'those' for things that are far away.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Substitution Game
fun_activity.instructions: Write a short paragraph about your best friend using only their name. Then, rewrite the paragraph and replace their name with the correct pronouns!

quick_recap: ⭐ Pronouns take the place of nouns to avoid boring repetition.
⭐ Personal pronouns (I, he, they) represent specific people or things.
⭐ Possessive pronouns show ownership, and Demonstrative pronouns point things out.
